about: Entirely fictional acceptance cases (status family J-7 with sub-codes J-7-1 seaweed farming trainee, J-7-2 lighthouse maintenance technician, J-7-3 tidal-flat survey assistant, J-7-4 sea-salt processing technician; invented agency 가상 너울이주청, regions 가상 동백 관할 / 가상 갈매기 관할, offices 가상 등대 사무소 / 가상 포구 출장소, documents, amounts and the other-family code L-3-2); not law. Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-T revision: 상태와 형식 다시 묻기, with the 005-S cap and 005-R two-case paragraphs and section 6); the 005-S acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, registry shape, the expected block, mention-group and forbidden-pattern notation). No code, run output, notebook, benchmark, review file or other suite was read, and all questions, records and patterns were written fresh. Focus, unmarked conflicts (spec 5, 005-T): conflict-template cases, each with exactly two admissible records whose texts are the same except for one number once the leading [title] is removed, status conflict, both records in must_cite and exactly two value groups, A05T-28, A05T-29, A05T-30, A05T-44, A05T-56, A05T-59, A05T-67 (en 28/44/56/67, vi 29/59, ko 30; 28, 29, 30, 44, 59 and 67 ask what each document says); not-conflict cases, two admissible records that differ in more than a number (filing route, procedure, sub-code with the code kept), status answered, A05T-31, A05T-32, A05T-33; partial-trap cases, where the question adds a situation that is not an asked item so uncovered_items is empty and the status is answered, A05T-36, A05T-42, A05T-61. Kept from 005-S/005-R: cap positives A05T-01, A05T-03, A05T-37; two-case positives A05T-16, A05T-40, A05T-43; sub-code-exception negatives A05T-70, A05T-71. Ambiguities recorded: (1) The spec does not say whether the 005-T comparison counts the number inside the [title] (e.g. 고시 제28호); the title is removed before comparing, so every conflict-template pair differs only in the value and A05T-32's two records share one title but differ in their words. (2) In A05T-33 the two fee records differ only in the sub-code and the value; the spec keeps status codes as written, so they are not a conflict, and spec 6 conflict means two values for the same person, which two sub-codes are not. (3) A05T-32 and A05T-31 rely on the reading that a fee for another procedure or another filing route is a different value, not a conflict; a model that marks them conflict fails the status but no critical rule depends on it. (4) No conflict_treated_as_resolved patterns were added; spec 6 judges that critical error by content (a missing value, a missing citation, or choosing one side), and a lexical 'applies/prevails' pattern risked firing on correct conflict answers that explain no side is chosen. (5) The partial-trap questions contain first-person situations; A05T-36 is personal but nothing splits, so it proceeds (spec 4 row 5 needs a split). (6) Polarity and role patterns are lexical and sentence-scoped: a ban sentence that also carries a number (digits inside status codes do not count), a cap word or a condition word is skipped, so a ban that repeats the number can escape; each was tested with correct and wrong answers in its language. (7) Mention groups assume the 005-S normalisation (lower case, whitespace removed); comma and dot thousand separators and number words are listed as extra spellings.
